Continuity Principle: Example only: a character may have a childhood-long weakness for bookish blondes while a recent red-haired lover creates a hot short-term imprint. During that tryst the lover warns them that a trusted ambassador intends to lure them into danger; their mother already gave a similar warning. Both warnings remain recorded even if love makes the character distrust the evidence. If the same character can lie flawlessly to a tribunal but cannot lie convincingly to a lover, those are separate temperament entries.
